Know before you go

  1. Carry water

    A liter for every two hours of hiking, more in July. Lake and stream water has to be filtered.

  2. Stay on the trail

    Shortcuts kill meadow plants that take twenty years to grow back. Also, we find lost people a lot faster when they stayed on a trail.

  3. Lock up your food

    Use the bear locker at your site. Coolers and tents don't count.

  4. Make noise on blind corners

    Bears would rather hear you coming. Talk, clap, sing badly.

  5. Check conditions

    Weather at the pass can turn in an hour. Call the ranger line or stop at a station before you head up.

  6. Sign the trail register

    Sign in at the trailhead and sign out when you're back. If you don't sign out, we come looking.

ECHO BASIN PARK AUTHORITY. Internal, do not post.

To: all district staff
From: I. Okafor
Date: Sept. 13
Re: dusk procedure (replaces yesterday’s)

  1. Everybody indoors by dusk. That includes search teams. I know.
  2. No names on the radio, post numbers only. It's picked up eleven names so far and it uses them.
  3. When you talk to visitors or pose for photos, keep your back to the trees. It comes closer when somebody is looking at it.
  4. Log the bark and crown damage as wind. Log the height as forty feet. It's taller than that. Sam thinks it crouches to get under the canopy.
  5. If a visitor reports a fifth echo, get them inside and don't tell them the fifth one was their own voice.
  6. Knock at door height and say the room number. Guests have been told anything else isn't us.

Ines, it was at the lodge last night. Every window on the lake side at the same time, looking in from above. It doesn't need the door. I'm going up to measure anyway. S.

FILED
